events.content:
I want a small app for keeping track of the books I'm reading.

When I open it I want to see what I'm currently reading and what I've finished. I want to add a book from a form, mark one as finished, and click through to a book to see its title, author and my notes. I'd like to be able to send someone a link to a single book.

Nothing fancy and no accounts. Skip the database, save the books to a JSON file so they're still there after a restart.
I’ll inspect the existing project, then build the book list, add form, finish action, and shareable book pages using JSON-file storage.

args.content:
# Between Pages

A small, account-free reading tracker. Add books with a title, author, and notes; see what you're reading and what you've finished; mark books finished; and share a direct link to any book.

## Run it

Requires Node.js 18 or newer.

```sh
npm start
```

Open http://localhost:3000. To use a different port, set `PORT` (for example, `PORT=8080 npm start`). For development, `npm run dev` restarts the server when code changes.

Books are stored in `data/books.json`, created automatically when the first book is added. Keep that file to preserve your shelf across restarts, and back it up if needed. No database or account setup is required. If you host the app for others to access by link, use a host with persistent filesystem storage; ephemeral/serverless filesystems will not preserve the JSON file. With no accounts, anyone who can access the app can see and add books or mark them finished.

## Checks

```sh
npm test
npm run build
```

events.content:
Built the reading tracker. It shows currently reading and finished books, lets you add a book with notes, mark it finished, and open a shareable page for each book. Books are saved to `data/books.json` and survive a restart.

Run `npm start`, then open http://localhost:3000. A link will work for someone else only if they can reach the host running the app; with no accounts, anyone with access can view or change the shelf.

Checks passed: `npm test && npm run build` (exit 0; 2 tests passed, including persistence after restart). An `npm start` smoke test returned HTTP 200 for the library and add-book pages. Visual appearance wasn’t browser-tested.
